SMTO-CMP-0035 — The AI said the task failed, but none of its steps failed

GUID: f815a081-c28a-4b3a-8bf6-db5b546e290a
Slug: completion-unsupported-failed-status
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The AI tried to end the task as failed, but none of its steps actually failed. SMTO asked it to describe what is really unfinished instead. Work already done is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the task still shows Running, wait. SMTO has asked the AI to describe the unfinished part accurately. An accurate description tells you what's missing, instead of a failure that didn't happen.
  2. When it stops, read the AI's last reply for what it couldn't do, such as missing access, a missing file or an unclear request. That reason, not a failed step, is what's holding the task back.
  3. Provide what's missing or clarify your request in a new message, and ask SMTO to continue from where it stopped. Once the real blocker is sorted out, SMTO can finish the rest without redoing finished steps.

What success looks like

  • The task ends with a status and reason that match what happened, such as Completed, or Partial · resumable with a clear explanation.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't restart the whole task; the steps that already worked would run again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A failed terminal declaration was rejected because no retained result has status error, failed or outcome_unknown, and no completed process observation supports reporting failure.

What this means

  • A failed terminal declaration has no retained error/failed/unknown operation or completed process observation that supports reporting that status. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • A failed terminal declaration has no retained error/failed/unknown operation or completed process observation that supports reporting that status.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect actual receipts and choose the supported status that describes unresolved work truthfully.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the statuses in state.results for the run. The model should declare partial or blocked with an accurate description of the unresolved work, or obtain a real failing observation if failure is the true outcome; this check is enforced through the completion.receipt_verification Agent Check (Verify completion evidence).
  • Use a supported status and describe the unresolved work accurately.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The terminal status is grounded in retained operation evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
